column1: # Things the archive must be able to answer, checked against the live database.
# Each row is something Pippijn knows independently of the archive (his memory,
# his phone, the Chat UI), so a query that stops returning it means the pipeline
# lost something. Never derive a row from the database: that only tests that the
# archive agrees with itself. A row must be true now, not expected to become
# true, or it fails without any loss.
# Rows that name a person, a conversation or what somebody said go in
# known_truths.private.tsv, which git-crypt encrypts in the public repo.
# Run:  tools/check_known_truths.py
# Format: name <TAB> expected <TAB> sql
name
gchat: reactions name who reacted
telegram: calls keep how they ended, not just that they happened
column3: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM telegram_calls WHERE reason IS NOT NULL

column1: telegram: the longest call is most of an hour, not a flag
column3: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM telegram_calls WHERE duration_s > 3000

column1: telegram: reactions name a person
column3: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM telegram_reaction_authors WHERE removed_at IS NULL

column1: telegram: a forward remembers when the original was written
column3: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM telegram_messages WHERE fwd_date IS NOT NULL

column1: telegram: albums are reconstructable
column3: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT grouped_id) FROM telegram_messages WHERE grouped_id IS NOT NULL

column1: signal: a read receipt records WHEN, not just that it happened
column3: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM signal_receipts WHERE kind='read' AND when_ts > 0

column1: signal: a reaction knows who made it
column3: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM reactions WHERE author_uuid IS NOT NULL AND author_uuid <> ''

column1: irc: the archive goes back to 2013
column3: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM irc_messages WHERE sent_at < '2014-01-01' LIMIT 1
